title: Counting Interest Bridge Days on a Ridgeline Consumer Credit Account — Training Note
content:
**What the bridge days are.** In a Ridgeline Consumer Credit good-standing amount, the bridge days are counted in calendar days to today, from a starting day set by the most recent payment credited on the account, measured against the latest statement's due date:

| Most recent payment credited on the account | Bridge days run from |
|---|---|
| no payment has ever been credited, or the most recent payment came more than 30 days before the latest statement's due date | the latest statement date |
| the most recent payment came 15 to 30 days before that due date | the date of that most recent payment |
| otherwise — fewer than 15 days before the due date, on it, or after it | the latest statement's due date |

An account on which no payment has ever been credited is treated as if its most recent payment came 9999 days before the due date, which places it in the first row.

## Boundary dates (hypothetical: statement dated 31 May, due date 25 June, today 7 July)

| Most recent payment credited | Days before the due date | Bridge days from | Bridge days |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25 May | 31 | 31 May, the statement date | 37 |
| 26 May | 30 | 26 May, the payment date | 42 |
| 10 June | 15 | 10 June, the payment date | 27 |
| 11 June | 14 | 25 June, the due date | 12 |
| 28 June | after the due date | 25 June, the due date | 12 |
| none ever | — | 31 May, the statement date | 37 |

**Questions a new representative asks.** *Is the most recent payment limited to the last month?* No; it is the most recent payment credited on the account at any time. *Do the days include today?* They are the calendar days from the starting day to today, so a start of 25 June and a today of 7 July give 12.
